title: Stone Game IX
summary: Alice and Bob play a game with stones.
statement: Alice and Bob play a game with stones. Each stone has a value. Alice starts. Players take turns removing a stone. A player loses if the sum of removed stones' values is divisible by 3. Bob wins if all stones are removed. Assuming optimal play, return true if Alice wins, false if Bob wins.
constraints: Players alternately remove a stone; the mover loses immediately when the running sum becomes divisible by three.
Bob wins if all stones are removed; return whether Alice wins under optimal play.
reference_solution:
def alice_wins_stone_game_nine(stones):
    counts=[0,0,0]
    for value in stones:counts[value%3]+=1
    if counts[0]%2==0:return counts[1]>0 and counts[2]>0
    return abs(counts[1]-counts[2])>2

hints: Only each stone’s residue modulo three matters.
Count residues zero, one, and two; residue-zero parity changes whose strategy applies, while residues one and two must be balanced differently.
If count0 even require both count1 and count2; if odd require abs(count1-count2)>2.
Alternating residues one and two avoids a zero sum; analyzing which side runs out, with zero moves swapping turns, yields these necessary and sufficient cases.

tests.explanation: Alice can remove either residue and force Bob into the losing divisible-by-three move.
Alice removes the only stone without reaching a divisible sum, so exhaustion awards Bob the win.
